title: Russian forces take Sievierodonetsk in Luhansk Oblast
body:
Russian forces took control of Sievierodonetsk, in Ukraine's Luhansk region, on Saturday 25 June 2022, four months after the invasion began. The city had a prewar population of about 100,000 and had endured weeks of heavy bombardment. Ukrainian fighters held out at the Azot chemical plant with hundreds of civilians before Ukraine ordered a retreat.

Luhansk governor Serhiy Haidai said the withdrawal was due to the destruction of defensive structures, and that Ukraine lost no fighters during it. He said more than 10,000 people remained in the city, mostly those who chose to stay, although authorities had urged evacuation for three months. The city measures roughly four kilometres by four kilometres.

Attention turned to Lysychansk, Sievierodonetsk's twin city across the Seversky Donets River, which became the only town in Luhansk still under Ukrainian control. Haidai said it was shelled more than 150 times in one day, that Russian forces were trying to encircle it, and that Ukrainian troops would hold it "for as long as possible". He said all troops from Sievierodonetsk had moved there. If Russia captured Lysychansk it would control all of Luhansk, which together with Donetsk makes up the Donbas.
